label: Pitch
summary: Pitch is what we perceive as a high or a deep voice. Technically it is the perceived fundamental frequency, determined by the physical characteristics of a speaker's vocal folds. Shorter, thinner vocal folds vibrate faster and produce higher pitched voices.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike introduces pitch as part of a broader primer on speech and prosody aimed at conversation designers working with SSML. She uses it to challenge a common assumption: pitch alone does not determine whether a voice is perceived as male or female, because speech style plays a role too. She frames this as useful news for voice designers, suggesting it opens up possibilities for crafting a more varied and inclusive palette of voices.
open_questions: How exactly does speech style interact with pitch in shaping perceived gender, and what does that mean concretely for SSML tagging choices?
What other prosodic properties beyond pitch matter most when designing inclusive or gender-neutral voice assistants?
